content.title: How to watch Timberwolves at Warriors tonight: game preview, injury updates and TV and streaming info | Minnesota Timberwolves
content.text: The Minnesota Timberwolves are back in action Friday with a road matchup against the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco.The Wolves are coming off a 153-128 road loss to the LA Clippers on Wednesday. Anthony Edwards lead the team with 36 points and five assists.Sixth in the West at 40-26, the Wolves are 6-4 in their last 10 games and 18-14 on the road. Minnesota is ranked 11th on defense (113.0 defensive rating) and 12th on offense (116.1 offensive rating).Here’s what to know going into Friday’s Timberwolves vs. Warriors matchup, starting with where to watch or stream and who is on the injury report.How to watch, stream & listen to Timberwolves at WarriorsDate: Friday, March 13Start Time: 9 PM CTTV Channel/Live Stream: Prime VideoRadio: iHeartRadio | Timberwolves app | KFAN 100.3Where: Chase Center | San Francisco, CAWolves at Warriors tips off at 9 PM on Friday, March 13, at Chase Center in San Francisco. The game will be broadcast and streamed on Prime Video.Injury ReportNote: Tonight's injury report will be updated before the start of the game.Timberwolves Out: Joan Beringer, Enrique Freeman & Zyon PullinJoan Beringer (G League On Assignment), Enrique Freeman (G League Two-Way) and Zyon Pullin (G League Two-Way) are out.WarriorsOut: Jimmy Butler III, Draymond Green, Stephen Curry & Moses MoodyJimmy Butler III (Right ACL Surgery), Draymond Green (Left Low Back Injury Management), Stephen Curry (Right Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome) and Moses Moody (Right Wrist Sprain) are out.Jerseys Timberwolves: Icon EditionWarriors: Association EditionThe Wolves will be wearing their blue Icon Edition uniforms against the Warriors, who will be in their white Association Edition uniforms.What to know about the WarriorsNinth in the West at 32–33, Golden State enters Friday on a three-game losing streak and is 3–7 over their last 10. The Warriors are 19–14 at home.Golden State ranks 12th in defense (113.1 defensive rating) and 17th in offense (114.1 offensive rating).Friday marks the fourth and final meeting between Golden State and Minnesota this season. The Wolves lead the series 2–1.With several key players sidelined, Golden State's rotation will likely include Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford, Gui Santos, Brandin Podziemski, Pat Spencer, De’Anthony Melton, Quinten Post & Gary Payton II.
